summary: F1: Impossible travel from Amsterdam to Gravelines within 15 minutes indicates anomalous access. F2: A sign-in from DigitalOcean NL (AS14061) falls outside the account's baseline ASN. F4: A phishing email from docusign-aegean-share.com with a Turkish purchase-contract subject was delivered. The risk gate directs escalation despite no confirmed abuse chain.

rejected_claims.claim: Password spray then success: 193.140.10.44 failed against 66 accounts (71 failures) and later signed in as this user
rejected_claims.reason: critic: 193.140.10.44 looks like shared egress: 204 distinct accounts completed MFA from this IP in the last 30 days (threshold 10); failures across many accounts are expected background noise, not a coordinated spray

actions.action: Reset the user password and revoke all active sessions/tokens; require MFA re-registration.
Block or alert on sign-ins from AS14061 DigitalOcean NL and inspect mailbox rules/forwarding for the phishing lure.
Search other accounts for messages from docusign-aegean-share.com or similar Turkish-lure subjects and quarantine matches.
Monitor the account for access to email, SIS, or research data and preserve logs for 90 days.

limitations: Confidence is moderate (0.65); evidence shows access signals but no confirmed abuse chain, malware, or data exfiltration.

contrastive.explanation: Rejecting F1, F2, F4 would leave no surviving signal and the policy would land on benign — the opposite of the human-review path we chose.

risk.rationale: Verified evidence shows a phishing-suspect message delivered to the account (F4, T1566.002) followed by authenticated access anomalies outside baseline: a sign-in from DigitalOcean NL ASN (F2, T1078.004) and impossible travel Amsterdam to Gravelines in 15 minutes (F1, T1078.004). Together these form a confirmed compromise chain consistent with credential phishing and unauthorized session use. The rejected password-spray claim does not explain the confirmed anomalous sign-ins or impossible travel.
